summary: Discover effective strategies for rural health systems and community health development. Enroll in our training to empower your community and improve health.
lede: Rural health training helps health and community-development professionals plan and strengthen accessible, reliable community services. It covers mapping system gaps, supporting community health worker programs, planning inclusive outreach and referral pathways, and using routine data and quality-improvement cycles to guide decisions. Participants also practice coordinating stakeholders and shaping practical development plans around constraints such as distance, staffing, supplies, and budgets.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who are tasked with strengthening or managing community health and rural service delivery systems.
audience: Public sector health managers and county/district health
NGO program managers and project coordinators
Community health focal persons and CHW supervisors
Donor-funded project officers and grant managers
Monitoring and evaluation professionals in health programs
WASH, nutrition, maternal and child health specialists
Health communication and SBC (social behavior change)
outcomes: Health Data Use For Decision Making
modules: Foundations of Rural Health Systems and Community Health Development
Mapping Rural Health System Building Blocks
Community Health Structures and CHW Program Design
Equity, Gender, and Inclusive Access in Rural Health
Outreach Planning and Last-Mile Service Delivery
Referral Pathways and Continuity of Care
Supply Chains, Essential Medicines, and Basic Equipment Readiness
Data for Decision-Making, Not Just Reporting
Quality Improvement in Rural Health Services
Designing a Results-Driven Community Health Development Plan
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of health systems and community health concepts. Prior experience in project management or health program implementation is beneficial.
